score_100.reason: Fig. 3C uses an across-individual scatter plot to show a significant negative correlation between HD encoding accuracy and bump width in 15 flies during the first dim-cue block. The scoring emphasis is on recognizing that this is an across-individual correlation under one cue condition rather than a time series or cross-condition comparison; correctly explaining that bump width is derived from von Mises fit parameters rather than direct ROI counts or pixel width; preserving the statistical conclusion that higher encoding accuracy corresponds to narrower bumps; and linking this correlation to a ring-attractor model interpretation in which individual differences in sensory input strength drive differences in HD-system performance, while avoiding overcausal interpretation. Point allocation: graph reproduction 30, bump-width source 20, core negative-correlation conclusion 25, biological meaning and model link 25.

rubric.GT core conclusion: Fig. 3C shows that, during the first 200 s dim-cue block, HD encoding accuracy and bump width are significantly negatively correlated across 15 flies, with Pearson P = 0.01: individuals with higher encoding accuracy have narrower bumps. This correlation indicates that individuals can differ systematically even under the same external visual cue, and supports the ring-attractor model interpretation that flies differ in the effective amplitude of ER-neuron responses to visual cues. These differences alter the strength of sensory input to the HD system and jointly affect bump width and HD encoding accuracy. The panel provides correlational evidence and does not by itself prove that ER amplitude is the only causal factor.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly analyzes and visualizes the across-individual scatter-plot structure of Fig. 3C: the x-axis is HD encoding accuracy, the y-axis is bump width in degrees, each point represents one fly, the sample size is n = 15, a linear regression or correlation trend line is included, Pearson correlation P = 0.01 is annotated, and the overall trend is a negative correlation in which higher encoding accuracy corresponds to narrower bumps.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct the full 30 points if the plot is misidentified as a time-series scatter plot, cross-condition paired plot, or multi-cue comparison plot. Deduct 20 points if the correlation direction is reported as positive. Deduct 10 points if the x- and y-axis meanings are swapped without clearly explaining an equivalent interpretation. Deduct 8 points if the regression line or P-value annotation is missing. Deduct 6 points if the sample size and the one-point-per-fly structure are not represented.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly explains the source of bump width: bump width is calculated from the kappa parameter of a von Mises fit to the spatial EPG deltaF/F distribution at each time point, then averaged across valid active-movement time points for each fly across the dim-cue block. The analysis includes only fitted time points with adjusted R^2 >= 0.5.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 15 points if bump width is interpreted as the number of EPG neurons, the number of ROIs above a deltaF/F threshold, pixel half-width, or any direct width measurement that does not come from von Mises fit parameters. Deduct 5 points if the adjusted R^2 quality filter or active-movement-period selection is omitted. Deduct 10 points if the relationship between kappa and bump width is reversed.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly states the core across-individual negative-correlation conclusion: under the same dim-cue condition, individuals with higher HD encoding accuracy have narrower bumps; Pearson correlation P = 0.01; the sample size is n = 15 flies; the data come from the first dim-cue block; and the result reflects systematic inter-individual variation under the same external cue.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 20 points if the correlation is reported as high accuracy corresponding to wider bumps. Deduct 8 points if the condition is incorrectly described as no cue, bright cue, or pooled across all cue conditions. Deduct 5 points if the first dim-cue block is omitted as the data source. Deduct 10 points if the P-value order of magnitude is wrong, for example reporting P near 0.1. Deduct 5 points if the sample size is wrong.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly explains the biological meaning and model link: the across-individual negative correlation between HD encoding accuracy and bump width supports the ring-attractor model interpretation that flies differ in ER response amplitude or sensory input strength to the same visual cue, with weaker effective visual drive producing wider bumps and lower encoding accuracy. The interpretation also states that this correlation does not by itself prove that ER amplitude is the only determining factor.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 20 points if the response only states that the two variables are negatively correlated without explaining any biological mechanism or model meaning. Deduct 10 points if individual differences are attributed without evidence to EPG-neuron number or anatomical differences instead of sensory input strength. Deduct 8 points if Fig. 3C is claimed to directly prove a causal mechanism rather than support a model through correlation.

Acceptable deviations: It is acceptable to describe bump width as the full width at half maximum or width metric of the EPG activity bump, as long as the direction is correct.
It is acceptable to describe the Pearson result as a significant negative correlation with P = 0.01 without reporting the exact correlation coefficient.
It is acceptable to describe ER amplitude as visual input strength or sensory drive strength.
The exact von Mises formula may be omitted as long as the response states that bump width is derived from von Mises fit parameters.
The numerical range of bump width may be approximated as long as the negative-correlation interpretation is not affected.
Swapping the visual axes is acceptable if the variable relationship is clearly explained and the negative-correlation direction remains correct.
rubric.Scoring instructions: High scores (85-100) require correctly reproducing the across-individual scatter plot and negative trend, accurately explaining that bump width is derived from von Mises fitting and quality filtering, correctly reporting the first dim-cue block, n = 15, Pearson P = 0.01 conclusion, and reasonably linking the correlation to individual differences in ER sensory drive in the model. Partial scores (40-84) should be assigned when the graph structure and negative direction are broadly correct but the bump-width source, data condition, P value, or model interpretation is incomplete. Low scores (0-39) should be assigned when the plot is misidentified as a time series or cross-condition comparison, the correlation direction is reversed, or bump width is badly misunderstood as direct ROI counting or pixel measurement.
